pr_title: Fix closing of decorated watcher channel on timeout
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

Fixes #102464

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Adds integration test exercising service-websocket watch testcase described in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/102464#issuecomment-853048131

correctly captured the failure with service websocket watches not closing:
```
    watch_timeout_test.go:139: hit timeout before connection closed
--- FAIL: TestWebsocketWatchClientTimeout (20.58s)
    --- PASS: TestWebsocketWatchClientTimeout/configmaps (5.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestWebsocketWatchClientTimeout/services (10.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration/apimachinery	22.514s
```


```release-note
Fixes regression in 1.20 with websocket-based watches of Service objects not closing correctly on timeout
```

issue_context.title: Watch of Service resource with WebSocket does not timeout appropriately
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:

Using the Fabric8 client, which defaults to using WebSockets for Watches, I established a Watch on Service resources.  After the timeout (implicit or explicit) rather than the WebSocket seeing a close control frame or even an EOF it continued to be open and fulfill ping/pong requests - but no Service events are sent.

#### What you expected to happen:

The WebSocket would close.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Create a WebSocket based Watch with the ListOptions timeoutSeconds set on the Service resource along with a steady production of Service events, such as create/delete of a dummy Service.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):

Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"19", GitVersion:"v1.19.0", GitCommit:"ffd6836", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-10-27T05:15:27Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.0", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"20", GitVersion:"v1.20.2", GitCommit:"faecb196815e248d3ecfb03c680a4507229c2a56", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-01-13T13:20:00Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

The behavior has been seen in both local minikube and OpenShift distributions based upon Kubernetes 1.20.

- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):

Fedora 33
comments: Is this the same issue as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/85548 ?

> Is this the same issue as #85548 ?

It could be related, but in that case the client is calling close.  In this case we expect the server to initiate the close.

A couple of things were discussed when we triaged this issue:
a) we need to involve the Fabric8 team (~java client?)
b) We don't always default to Websocket, in fact we discussed discontinuing it
c) But the code is still there, so it's allowed for now and we should support it.

Not sure what to do next @lavalamp @deads2k

a) no, it sounds like an apiserver problem, it should be reproducible with a go client in a test.
b) If anything, we should standardize on websockets. Brower based clients depend on them. And when/if we get rid of SPDY, websockets are the replacement.

This may be relevant to @caesarxuchao's interests.

> a) no, it sounds like an apiserver problem, it should be reproducible with a go client in a test.

I didn't see an option to use websockets with the go client https://github.com/fabric8io/kubernetes-client/issues/3177#issuecomment-850464286 the impl is at https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/56494c9682c414b74bb83639bd6890feed82d307/rest/request.go#L671

Is there another code path or go client that will use a websocket for Watches?

Technically I didn't say *our* go client, just *a* go client. 😅 I just had in mind using the raw websockets library.

...we must be testing the websocket watches *somehow*?
Yeah, we should absolutely be able to stick that in a unit / integration test somewhere, thanks!

opened in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102539

configmap watch works correctly, service watch hits timeout without the server closing the connection
I suspect the issue is in newDecoratedWatcher. Services implement a decorator and configmaps don't.
yup, the request context wasn't propagated to the decorated watcher

Service decorator was added in 1.20 in 6675eba3eff1c8e565c4060a9c1396f75da7cc3e

Fix with unit and integration test in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102539

Will pick to 1.21 and 1.20 once merged

review_comments: this ensures the invariant that resultCh is closed when run() returns

This assumed the underlying watcher closed when it sent an error event. Even if all known watcher implementations do both of those things together, the decorating layer should not infer closing from an error event. The decoratedWatcher pipe should be dumb and merely propagate events, decorating non-error events, until the underlying watcher closes its result channel or the context is cancelled
When is this assumption not true today?  can you give an example?  Maybe this is just cleanup overall?
edited my comment to clarify... all known watcher implementations do close after sending an error, but as a distinct operation that should be handled by the "channel closed" case above
directly call Stop on the underlying watcher, otherwise an always ready underlying watcher result channel can win the `select` race in the `run` loop and we might never hit the ctx.Done() case
always stop the underlying watcher if our context is done
